Prevention: Deeply plough before and after cropping to expose cutworms to sun and natural enemies
Use good agronomic and cultural methods to produce strong plants that can tolerate some cutworms.
Prepare land early, this is, at least two weeks before planting.
Plant early, this is, mid to end of
Avoid low dump areas of the field that have poor drainage.
Control weeds in fall and early season.
Rotate with non- host plants such as cotton.
Monitoring: Scout for cutworm larvae as soon as crop emerges and continue twice weekly until plant reaches knee height.
Monitor early morning as larvae go deeper into soil during the day.
Look for 2 to 4 cm long c-shaped thick soft larvae around freshly damaged plants:
Examine at least 2 series of 20 consecutive plants.
Record number of plants that are cut, wilted or showing signs of feeding on lower leaves.
Scratch soil off plant roots to check for cutworms.
Control action may be required when 3% or more plants are cut/ damaged and one or more cutworms are found near or below damaged plants.
If available use pheromone or black light traps to monitor cutworm moth (appears reddish to blackish with front wings that are brown to black).
Direct Control: Hand pick larvae from the soil at night or early in the morning (during the day they are hidden in the soil)
Chop 30 -40 hot peppers or 1/2 litres of hot pepper powder into a 10 litre big bucket of warm water (not boiling).
Remove the pepper and dilute with 10 litres of cold water in the knapsack sprayer.
Spray in the evening directly on the soil around the stem of seedlings or young plants until soil is wet.

Restrictions
Only apply products when verified by monitoring.
Spray in the evening directly on to the soil around stems of young plantings.
Larvae will crawl near plant stem at night.
When using a pesticide (even a botanical home-brew), always wear protective clothing.
Follow the instructions on the product label, such as dosage, timing of application, pre-harvest interval, max number of sprays, restricted re-entry interval.
Do not empty into drains.

II pesticides might not be allowed in local
IPM schemes.
Always consult recent list of registered pesticides (ZEMA).
